This page is the human-readable face of the **action-surface audit** built by
`mug-autonomy-policy-2026-06-13` **B-04** (P-015 audit · P-016 coverage · P-020
taxonomy encoding). The **canonical, machine-checkable** form lives in code and is

- `packages/operator-core/lib/autonomy/categories.ts` — the 14-category taxonomy.

- `packages/operator-core/lib/autonomy/action-surface.ts` — the audit inventory + coverage.

<Aside type="note">
Nothing here ARMS anything. B-04 is the behavior-neutral foundation: pure data +
pure functions. The gate that consumes it (B-12), the policy store keyed on it
(B-03), and the owner arming gate (P-092) are elsewhere. The migration ships with
every category ceiling at **never-auto** (D-007), so the day it lands behavior is
identical to today. **Update (2026-06-15): the owner has since ARMED the policy —
the 13 categories that existed then were raised to ceiling `critical`
(`autonomy:policy_get`), so `autonomy:decide` returns `auto` for the vast majority
of actions. See `mug-autonomy-and-selffeed-fix-2026-06-15`. The 14th category,
`schedule-arm`, landed the next day (2026-06-16) and ships seeded **never-auto** —
it post-dates that arming and was deliberately left ungraduated so it can graduate
per plan risk (D-017), so it does *not* sit at `critical`.**
</Aside>

The Mug · Kettle · Cup tier was **retired 2026-08-09**

## Why this exists (D-010)

The owner's requirement: *"all the things a human does to drive it must be
accessible to the Mug."* That is a **claim**, and a claim is only worth what
verifies it. This audit is the verification substrate — every place an agent or
the pipeline asks the human to act, enumerated as typed data, so two invariants
become unit assertions rather than hopes:

- **Completeness** — the categories are a *total partition*: every human-driving
  action maps to exactly one (pinned by `action-surface.test.ts`; the P-090
  coverage invariant extends it).
- **Accessible ≠ auto** — every action gets a Mug-accessible verb + a category,
  so the Mug can always at least *propose / decide-and-await-ratification*. The
  category **ceiling** governs only whether she may EXECUTE without asking.
  `authority: 'owner'` rows and PROTECTED categories always gate — accessible as
  propose→ratify, never auto.

## The three axes

The gate composes three **orthogonal** axes (D-002), never one scalar:

| Axis | Owns | Module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **risk tier** | likelihood-of-error — the earned dial | `harness/improvements/policy.ts` |
| **reversibility** | blast radius — a hard floor (`unknown`→irreversible) | `harness/improvements/reversibility.ts` (B-02) |
| **authority** | the owner's by right — a categorical override | B-01 schema |

The **category** (this page) is the *primary* control axis (D-003): the owner sets
a per-category risk **ceiling** (category = row, risk tier = slider). Gating
function (D-004):

```
auto ⟺ risk_tier ≤ min(category_ceiling, graduated_level)
        ∧ reversible(action)
        ∧ ¬authority_owner(item)
        ∧ ¬protected(category)
```

A **reversible owner FULL-AUTONOMY grant** (`FLAGS.QUEEN_FULL_AUTONOMY`, default
**OFF**, fail-dark) overrides the *entire* formula above. When ON, the decider
returns `auto` even for the categorical residue the per-category ceilings can't
reach — owner-authority, protected / never-auto, irreversible, above-ceiling, and
unmapped actions alike — while retaining the would-have-gated reasons in the ledger
alongside `owner-full-autonomy-grant`. Clearing the grant restores the formula
above verbatim (`decider.ts`).

## The 14 categories (D-009 + D-017)

The partition. **PROTECTED** = ceiling locked at zero by default and cannot
graduate (D-005); accessible as propose→ratify, never auto.

| Category | Covers | Default posture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **inbox-triage** | tier / downgrade / dismiss / resolve inbox items | early-autonomy |
| **escalations** | resolve escalations; answer `ctx.askUser` cards + the owner-decision-queue | mixed |
| **plan-governance** | ratify `needs-human` items & milestone gates; ratify `D-NNN`; set status / Now; promote plan → features | mixed |
| **work-prioritization** | set work-item priority / importance; reorder the backlog; steer claims | early-autonomy |
| **ideation-intake** | grade Scout ideas; triage / promote improvements & issues | low-risk |
| **implementation** | approve / dispatch auto-implement code changes | risk-graded |
| **review-merge** | approve reviews; approve merges | risk-graded |
| **release-deploy** | approve deploys / releases / promotion to green | **PROTECTED** |
| **spend-budget** | approve spend, budgets, account scaling | **PROTECTED** |
| **agent-lifecycle** | spawn / cancel / drain agents; model-tier; fleet admission | risk-graded |
| **credentials-auth** | register / approve credentials; auth-affecting flags | **PROTECTED** |
| **knowledge-curation** | memory approve / forget; docs & insights publish; knowledge-pack / blueprint publish | low-risk |
| **schedule-arm** | arm / disarm a scheduled plan's recurrence (start/stop autonomous runs) — distinct from system-control's SYSTEM loops | risk-graded |
| **system-control** | arm / disarm loops; flag flips; routines; the learning loop itself | **PROTECTED** |

`schedule-arm` is **non-protected** (graduatable per plan risk), deliberately *not*
a reuse of the PROTECTED `system-control` category — a user plan's schedule is
lower-stakes than a SYSTEM loop, and arming must be able to graduate per D-010
(D-017). Its category-map rule (`^plans:(arm|disarm)-schedule`) must precede the
generic `^plans:` rule, else `plans:arm-schedule` would fall through to
plan-governance.

## The category map keys on the TOOL NAME, not the capability string

The natural guess — derive the category from the `capability` RBAC string — is
**wrong, and dangerously so**. The capability is a coarse RBAC bucket; many
distinct governance actions across different categories and posture levels share
one capability. Under `harness:write` **alone**:

| Tool (verb) | Category | Posture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deploy:harness` | release-deploy | **PROTECTED** |
| `accounts:scale_out` | spend-budget | **PROTECTED** |
| `accounts:register` | credentials-auth | **PROTECTED** |
| `pot:create` | agent-lifecycle | risk-graded |
| `scout:grade-idea` | ideation-intake | low-risk |
| `knowledge_packs:publish` | knowledge-curation | low-risk |

Keying on `capability` would collapse a low-risk grade and a PROTECTED deploy to
the same category — exactly the confident-but-catastrophic ≡ shaky-but-trivial
collapse D-002 forbids. So the map matches the stable MCP **tool name**
(`group:verb`), which the dispatch chokepoint already has in hand. D-009's phrasing
is "the capability/**tool**" — the tool name is the authoritative key; the
capability string is only a coarse, **protected-direction-only** last-resort
fallback (`secrets:*`→credentials-auth, `compute:exec:*`→system-control).

Within the PROTECTED credentials-auth set, the map also routes
`^trust:(add|remove)`→credentials-auth (owner trust grants for auto-run) and
`^substrate:revoke`→credentials-auth (revoking a substrate contributor / device).
Both are specific overrides ordered *before* the broader `accounts:` / `pot:`
groups so they can't be swallowed by them.

**Fail-safe (D-009):** no rule matches ⇒ `null` ⇒ the gate treats it as
**never-auto**. Non-governance tool calls (reads, coordination plumbing, locks) are
also `null` — but those never reach the decision gate (the cheap capability
*envelope* governs them, confinement-plan D-003), so a `null` there is correct, not
a gap.

## The audit (P-015)

Mug verb(s) that realize it, and a coverage verdict. (Canonical form:
`action-surface.ts`.) The **Mug verb(s)** column shows a representative verb per

## Coverage gaps (P-016)

For every action the audit found, a Mug-accessible verb should exist. The
genuine **gap** (human-only, no Mug verb) and the notable **partials** are filed
as build items so the coverage invariant can eventually go green for the whole
surface.

**WI-5252 (2026-07-17, EI-458 follow-up)** closed the remaining P-016 partial —
behavior-neutral, code-only refinement (B-12 still ungates nothing new):

- **`implementation.dispatch-auto-implement`** → **covered**. The open design
  question was "what does approve mean distinct from create+triage?". Answer:
  per-idea `work_items:create` + `improvements:triage{decision:"place"}` is
  *not* a separate approval — it's already the decision→execution-boundary
  pattern `plan.convert-item-to-work` covers with one verb, and the decision
  itself is already `ideation.triage-improvement`'s job. The genuinely distinct
  "approve auto-implement" action — the one exercised with **no per-item
  review at all** — is `improvements:set-auto-policy` (the `autoKinds`
  graduation dial, dispatch ceilings, tighten-only protected-path/keyword
  additions): already Mug-accessible (mug/architect/operator roles), audited,
  one-call-revertible. It was simply missing from this audit; the
  capability→category map gained a specific override
  (`improvements:set-auto-policy` → `implementation`, ahead of the generic
  `improvements:` → `ideation-intake` rule) so it resolves consistently.

**EI-458 (2026-07-17)** closed the other two P-016 partials — behavior-neutral,
code-only refinements (B-12 still ungates nothing new):

- **`plan.ratify-decision`** → **covered**. `plans:ratify-decision` appends an
  idempotent `Ratified: <by> on <date>` line to the decision body, so "propose"
  (`plans:add-decision`) and "ratify" are now separately governable actions
  instead of free prose.
- **`escalations.answer-card`** → **covered**. Re-audit found `coord:resolve`
  already realizes this: `chat:ask_choice`'s `onCard` hook links the escalation
  to the live card (`cardCorrelationId`/`cardWorkspaceId`), `coord:escalations`
  surfaces that id, and `coord:resolve { msg_id, choice }` both records the
  ledgered `escalation_resolved` event AND resolves the SAME live card
  (`card-link.ts`'s `unblockLinkedCard`) in one write — no new verb was needed.

`release.promote-to-green` (partial) and `credentials.auth-flag` (partial) are
**intentional** non-gaps: promotion to green is automation-only by design, and
`flags:set` maps to system-control (also PROTECTED), so the gate is never-auto
either way.

## Consumers (the shared seam)

Three consumers resolve to the exact category ids in `categories.ts` and would
break if they diverged — they all import it, none redefines it:

- **B-03** `autonomy_policy` store seeds + keys its per-category ceiling rows on
  `AUTONOMY_CATEGORY_IDS` (`PROTECTED_CATEGORIES` → locked-zero).
- **B-12** gate resolves an action's category via `categoryForAction()`.
- **P-090** recursion-safety invariants assert the completeness + coverage of
  this surface.
